title: Koko Eating Bananas
statement:
Koko loves bananas. There are `n` piles of them, and the guards come back in `h` hours. Koko picks an eating speed of `k` bananas per hour. Each hour she chooses one pile and eats `k` bananas from it. If the pile has fewer than `k` left, she eats all of them and does not start another pile that hour. Find the smallest whole speed `k` that lets her eat every banana within `h` hours.

The first line is the number of piles `n`, at least 1. The second line holds the `n` pile sizes, each from 1 to one billion. The third line is `h`, at least `n` and at most one billion, so some speed always works. Print the smallest speed `k`.

Input:

```text
4
3 6 7 11
8
```

Expected output:

```text
4
```
hints: If Koko can finish at some speed, she can also finish at any faster one. So the speeds from 1 up to the biggest pile switch from too slow to fast enough exactly once, and you can binary search for that switch.
Write a check for one speed that adds up the hours every pile takes. A pile of `p` bananas takes `p / k` hours rounded up, which in whole numbers is `(p + k - 1) / k`.
At slow speeds the total can pass two billion hours. Keep the sum in a 64-bit integer: `long` in Java, `long long` in C++, and `int64` in Go.
